stem: Meera's teacher asks her to explain why the broad, flat leaves of the money plant growing near her classroom window are good at making food. Which answer correctly justifies this?

options.text: Broad, flat leaves give a large surface to receive sunlight, so the chlorophyll in the leaf can make more food by photosynthesis.
Broad, flat leaves can make food even in complete darkness, because their shape alone is enough for photosynthesis.
Broad, flat leaves spread the sunlight more thinly, so they make less food than narrow leaves under the same light.
Broad, flat leaves capture more sunlight so that they can carry out respiration, which makes food for the plant.

teacher.key_rationale: Photosynthesis requires sunlight and chlorophyll; a broad, flat lamina maximises the light-receiving surface, making the leaf an efficient food-making site. A states this correctly. B omits the need for light, C reverses the surface-area relationship, and D wrongly attributes food-making to respiration.
